fields.meta_title: Reasonable Accommodation Request Form for HR | Emergent
fields.meta_description: What a reasonable accommodation request form should ask and leave off, plus an app that routes each request to HR and logs every meeting.
fields.h1: Build a Reasonable Accommodation Request Form
fields.hero_description: A reasonable accommodation request form records the change a person needs because of a disability. Emergent builds the form and the case log HR works from.
fields.features_heading: One Case File for Every Request
fields.features_subheading: A PDF records the request. Emergent's version sends it to the right person and logs the conversation that follows.
fields.feature_1:
Questions about the job, not the diagnosis

Asks which part of the job has become hard and what change would help. There is no diagnosis field, and the employee can answer in everyday words instead of legal terms.
fields.feature_2:
Routed to a coordinator, not the manager

Sends each request to the HR coordinator you name, stamped with the time it came in. Managers hear about an approved change once it is ready, never the reason behind it.
fields.feature_3:
A dated log of every meeting

Records each meeting with the employee and every option discussed, with the reason it was kept or ruled out. Whoever picks up the case later reads its whole history in one place.
fields.feature_4:
Provider forms only when they are needed

Sends a documentation request to the employee's health care provider when the coordinator asks for one. Replies go to a medical table kept apart from the personnel record.
fields.feature_5:
Reminders before a case goes quiet

Pings the coordinator in Slack or by email when a case has gone untouched for the days you set. The written decision goes to the employee from that same record, with a start date.
fields.feature_6:
Your code, in your GitHub repo

Exports the full codebase to your repository. Your engineers can connect it to the HR system you run through its API, or ask Emergent to build that sync with one more prompt.

fields.tab_content_1:
A request in her words, no diagnosis asked

Most requests arrive in plain words. A Northwind Freight dispatcher writes that 10-hour shifts at a fixed desk hurt her back, and asks for a sit-stand desk. The form records the task and the change. Dana Brooks, the accommodation coordinator, has it by 9:40 that morning, and her manager has not been copied.
fields.tab_content_2:
Both meetings logged before the lift decision

The interactive process is a conversation, and the app keeps its minutes. A warehouse lead can no longer lift more than 20 pounds. Dana meets him twice and logs two options: a lift-assist cart, or handing his loading to a teammate. The cart keeps him in his role, and the written decision goes out with a start date.
fields.tab_content_3:
The doctor's note stays out of the personnel file

Some needs are not obvious. An analyst asks to start at 10:00 instead of 8:00, and Dana sends a short provider form to her doctor. The reply is filed in a separate medical record, never in her personnel file. Her manager sees one line: start time 10:00, approved.
fields.tab_content_4:
Interpreter on Thursday, and the reason stays with HR

Applicants ask before the interview. A deaf candidate for a warehouse associate job uses the request link on the careers page to ask for an ASL interpreter. The recruiter gets a task to book one for Thursday at 2:00 PM. The interviewer's calendar invite says an interpreter will attend, with nothing about why.

fields.howto_title: How to Create an Accommodation Form
fields.howto_description: The form is the easy part. These seven steps cover who receives a request, what to ask, and the record HR keeps once the conversation starts.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask about the job, not the condition
fields.howto_step_1_des: Name one coordinator, usually in HR, and a backup. A request counts even when an employee mentions it to a supervisor in passing. Tell managers to pass anything they hear to the coordinator the same day.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask about the work itself: the duty that is now difficult and the adjustment the person has in mind. Leave diagnosis fields off the form. If documentation turns out to be necessary, request it later from a health care provider, and only when the need is not obvious.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Let people describe the need in plain words. A request does not have to mention the ADA or use the phrase reasonable accommodation. Treat a conversation or an email as a request too, and use the form to confirm it.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Write down each meeting, the options raised and why each one was kept or set aside. Give the employee's preferred option primary consideration. Where two options both work, the employer may choose between them, and the log shows how it decided.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Store provider replies in their own confidential file, never in the personnel record. A manager needs to know what changes and when it starts. The reason belongs with HR, and the app should never show it on the manager's screen.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Send a written decision that names the accommodation and the date it starts, plus who to contact if it stops working. When you turn a request down, state the reason and describe any alternative you offered instead.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Set a review date a month or two out to confirm the change is working. Equipment breaks and duties shift. A short check-in catches a problem before the employee has to file a second request for the same need.

claims_to_source: A request for reasonable accommodation does not need to be in writing or use the words reasonable accommodation; an employer may ask for a form but cannot ignore the initial request
Employer and employee should engage in an informal interactive process; the employee's preference gets primary consideration, but the employer may choose among effective accommodations
When the disability or need is not obvious, the employer may ask for reasonable documentation from an appropriate health care or rehabilitation professional

Reasonable accommodation may include modified schedules, equipment, interpreters, reassignment to a vacant position and leave; applicants are covered in the application process; undue hardship is the limit

Title I of the ADA covers employers with 15 or more employees; disability means an impairment that substantially limits a major life activity; compulsive gambling, kleptomania, pyromania and disorders from current illegal drug use are excluded; medical information is kept in separate confidential medical files
Executive Order 13164 requires federal agencies to have written procedures for reasonable accommodation requests, accept oral or written requests and give denials in writing with reasons
The Job Accommodation Network publishes sample accommodation request forms
